title: The issue of data scraping for Twitter 15 and Twitter 16 datasets
body:
您好，在数据集爬取方面我想请教几个问题，希望能够得到您的解答：
1.您之前提到，对社交网络中每个用户爬取2000个粉丝，以此构建他们之间的关系，但是我在爬取过程中发现，twitter15与16数据集中，有部分用户貌似已经注销无法爬取信息，请问这种情况您是如何处理的？
2.对于198个事件，每一个事件都确定了参与用户的情况下，举个例子，在a事件中有140人参与了事件传播，是通过对这140个参与用户都爬取2000个粉丝然后构建社交关系吗？

Translate to English:

Hello, I would like to ask you a few questions regarding dataset crawling and hope to receive your guidance:

You previously mentioned crawling 2,000 followers for each user on social networks to construct their relationships. However, during my crawling process, I noticed that in the Twitter15 and Twitter16 datasets, some users seem to have deactivated their accounts, making it impossible to retrieve their information. How did you handle such situations?

For the 198 events, once the participating users for each event have been identified, for example, if 140 people participated in event A, is the social relationship constructed by crawling 2,000 followers for each of these 140 participating users?
author: wwt12138

comments.body:
> You previously mentioned crawling 2,000 followers for each user on social networks to construct their relationships. However, during my crawling process, I noticed that in the Twitter15 and Twitter16 datasets, some users seem to have deactivated their accounts, making it impossible to retrieve their information. How did you handle such situations?

Indeed, such occurrences are possible, but they constitute a minority in the data I compile; therefore, I shall disregard them.

> For the 198 events, once the participating users for each event have been identified, for example, if 140 people participated in event A, is the social relationship constructed by crawling 2,000 followers for each of these 140 participating users?

The main idea is correctly understood, but it pertains to 'following' rather than 'followers'. due to cost constraints,  you may choose between them based on their respective quantities.

感谢您的解答，为了成本考虑，我自己尝试爬取了几个社交传播事件中参与事件传播的用户，构建了用户列表，爬取了用户列表中每个用户的1000个粉丝去构建社交关系，查找同时出现在用户的粉丝列表与用户列表中的用户id，发现很少有交集，社交传播网络中的几百个用户基本上很少存在直接关注的关系，即用1000个粉丝列表没能构建出社交关系，我想请教一下我的做法是否正确？

Translate to English:

Thank you for your response. To reduce costs, I attempted to crawl users who participated in the dissemination of several social events and built a user list. I then crawled 1,000 followers for each user in the list to construct social relationships. By checking for user IDs that appeared both in a user's follower list and in the user list, I found very little overlap. The few hundred users in the social dissemination network rarely had direct follow relationships. In other words, using 1,000 follower lists did not allow me to construct social connections. I would like to ask whether my approach is correct.

@wwt12138 
In larger topics such as politics and business, it is natural for the social network among users to be quite sparse. This is also one of the key reasons for introducing a recommendation system. If only a few hundred users have participated in the dissemination of the social events you are studying, I would recommend increasing the number of followers you crawl. (A helpful suggestion: For super users whose follower count far exceeds your crawling limit, you can establish their social relationships by checking whether they appear in other users' following lists.)

感谢您的解答，我按照您的建议，重新构建用户列表，收集参与用户的2000个following，构建彼此的相互关注关系。我发现在网络中，存在一些注销用户，以及一些无法收集信息的私密用户。除去这些用户后，能够收集到约几十条用户关系，形成网络中的边，这个边的数量是否有些少？您是否有表现较好的事件推荐？

Translate to English:

Thank you for your response. Following your suggestion, I rebuilt the user list, collected the 2,000 followings of participating users, and constructed mutual follow relationships. I found that some users had deactivated their accounts, while others were private and inaccessible. After excluding these users, I was able to collect only a few dozen user relationships, forming the edges in the network. Do you think this number of edges is too small? Do you have any recommendations for well-performing events?

The adequacy of the number of edges depends on the specific event. In real life, certain events spread primarily through platform recommendation algorithms, meaning the social network can be quite sparse. I suggest looking into entertainment news, as its spreaders are typically tightly connected fan communities, compared to those in politics or business.

title: Has the X dataset used in the paper been open-sourced? Specifically, does it include user info and user previous posts?
author: Micheallei

comments.body: Yeah, the X dataset, which includes the user ID and tweet ID, has been open-sourced in Twitter 15 and Twitter 16. We use the X API to get user information and previous tweets, but we can not open-source the specific user information and previous tweets because of privacy concerns. We recommend using X API or some open-sourced tools to get the information.

title: Change `repost` action to align with twitter Recsys
body: After discussing with @Redtides0 , I modified some details of the `repost` action implementation and default field in database to make it more compatible with Twitter's recommendation algorithm.
author: yiyiyi0817

comments.body:
> when you `quote_post`, checking `post_type` is also needed.

In the current main branch code, there is already a discussion on the classification of post types, so I did not modify the `quote_post` function in this PR. The current logic is that common posts will be directly quoted, while reposted and quoted posts will be quoted to the root post, just like the real Twitter.
And maybe we can also check each other again to ensure the robustness of the code.
